correctness.rationale: For a fixed triangle-free internal graph \(F\), realizability is equivalent to independent old-neighbourhoods and disjointness across internal edges. Summing over shore-colour assignments has weight \([I(F[X])I(F[Y])]^n\), with empty-neighbourhood overcount \(O_r(2^{(r-1)n})\). Proper two-colourings contribute \(2^{rn}\), whereas each nonproper colouring contributes at most \((3\cdot2^{r-2})^n\). For any non-bipartite internal graph, the highest shore weight corresponds to exactly one monochromatic edge; two or more monochromatic edges restrict each relevant base-vertex pattern to at most a fraction \(5/8\) of all assignments. This proves the sharp fixed-arity non-bipartite probability with leading coefficient \(A_r/\Theta_r\) and error \(O_r((5/8)^n)\), with positive coefficient at every arity at least five. The 32 pentagon assignments have bases 24 (ten times), 16 (ten), 15 (ten), and 11 (twice). Exact inclusion-exclusion proves the thirteen-term formula; an independent direct-neighbourhood method agrees at shore sizes zero through three. The twelve labelled pentagons give constant \(60/721\); independent six-vertex classification gives \(A_6=6120\). A conditional law of large numbers gives the two \(1/3\) endpoints on a uniform cycle edge and \(1/2\) at the other three vertices. Finite tests are checks of algebra only, not infinite proofs.
